ideas.title: Yesterday walks again
ideas.critique: Ghost doubles replaying the island's recorded past live next to the living is a new use of the frame log, and friends meeting themselves is funny. It shares Rewind's time-playback and Paths we wore's use of the history, but it is a different thing: it layers the past onto the present rather than undoing the present. Risk: ghosts of yesterday that do mundane things read as a rendering trick unless the encounter reactions are strong.

ideas.title: The tiny town that copies us
ideas.critique: A miniature society that mirrors the big island's events an hour late is a real change of scale and a clever echo of the island's own history. It needs real tiny life and several mirrored events to be more than a decorated stump, and it is only seen by looking closely. The earlier 'tiny island on the stump' pitch is the same seed, but this version adds the mirroring twist.

ideas.title: Pinchy's films
ideas.critique: Same core as the round 2 Pinchy's camera pitch, with the added step that its films reach the pages under its name. Giving a creature authorship of the site and the live view is a twist on who shows the island, though the wobbly low camera plus claw overlay is the plainest version. Judged as a reworded earlier idea, slightly stronger.

ideas.title: A language of their own
ideas.critique: Speech bubbles turned into a learnable glyph code with a dictionary on the site is a new relationship between the viewer and the creatures, and it grows over time. It is a permanent layer that translates existing actions into symbols, like the music layer, and it only works if the glyphs map to real state consistently. Strong if the dictionary is genuinely decodable; weak if it is decoration.
